newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse November turnover sharply up.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse November turnover sharply up.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) November turnover rose to 152.52 million dinars ($30 million) from 122.53 million in October, despite tight market liquidity, the bourse said on Tuesday.
The number of November transactions declined to 702 from 741 a month ago, the bourse reported.
BSE said November activity raised the 11-month total turnover on the BSE to 2.067 billion dinars. This compares to the total 1995 turnover of 717.6 million dinars.
Despite rising turnover, traders said overall liquidity of the market remained tight due to the central bank's decision to increase the reserve requirement to 15 from 10 percent.
The unpopular measure translated into a sharp decline in market liquidity, higher demand for fresh borrowing and drew minimal interest for the central bank short-term bonds, traders said.
But the central bank short-term bonds drew more interest as their maturity neared and the bank is expected to auction new tranche of bonds by the end of this week.
Buyer interest for wheat selling contracts reemerged towards the end of the month, ahead of the December 2 closing date for the securities sale, traders said.

Commercial paper traded 554 times for a volume of 85.12 million dinars, retaining a dominant share in the total monthly turnover. Those securities accounted for 56 percent of November turnover, down from 69 percent in October.
The National Bank of Yugoslavia short-term bonds accounted fo 26.8 million dinars or 18 percent of the total monthly turnover.
Wheat selling forward contracts followed with 20 deals worth 21.413 million dinars or 14 percent of the total.
Treasury bills generated 12 percent of the monthly total or 18.424 million dinars in 118 transactions, the bourse said. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
